title: Refeeding Syndrome Risk (NICE Criteria)
sources: NICE CG32 Nutrition support for adults (2006, updated); BAPEN refeeding guidance

changelog.change: Corrected minor thresholds to NICE — BMI < 18.5 (was 16–20) and weight loss > 10% in 3–6 months (was > 5% in 3 months); re-banded so a single minor criterion is not 'at risk' ([0–1] low, [2] at risk, [3+] high).

purpose: Stratifies the risk of refeeding syndrome before starting nutrition support, so calorie delivery and electrolyte replacement can be paced. NICE rule: ANY one MAJOR criterion, OR TWO OR MORE minor criteria, = at risk.

items.label: Low potassium, phosphate, or magnesium BEFORE feeding
History of alcohol misuse, or drugs — insulin, chemotherapy, antacids, or diuretics (minor)

interpretation.label: Not at risk by the NICE rule (no major criterion; fewer than 2 minor). Start nutrition support normally; still check K / PO4 / Mg over the first few days

At risk — 2 minor criteria. Start feeding at ~10 kcal/kg/day (increase to target over 4–7 days), give thiamine 200–300 mg + vitamin B co strong / a multivitamin BEFORE feeding and for the first 10 days, replace K / PO4 / Mg proactively, monitor electrolytes at least daily

High risk — ≥ 1 MAJOR criterion (BMI < 16, weight loss > 15% in 3–6 months, > 10 days negligible intake, or pre-feed low K / PO4 / Mg), or ≥ 3 minor. Start at 5–10 kcal/kg/day; if extremely high risk (BMI < 14, or negligible intake > 15 days) start at ~5 kcal/kg/day with cardiac monitoring. Thiamine before feeding, aggressive electrolyte replacement as you feed — do NOT fully correct electrolytes before starting

notes: Refeeding syndrome is driven by an insulin surge on carbohydrate delivery pulling phosphate, potassium, and magnesium intracellularly — causing arrhythmia, heart failure, rhabdomyolysis, seizures, and respiratory failure, typically in the first 72 h. Thiamine repletion prevents Wernicke's precipitated by the same carbohydrate load. Falling phosphate after feeding starts is the earliest lab marker.
buildNote: NICE criteria, additive helper. minor = 1 pt, major = 3 pts. Bands: 0–1 not at risk, 2 at risk (2 minor), ≥3 high (≥1 major or ≥3 minor).
